# Words Harper already knows and deliberately flags in *some* dialects.
#
# These are not gaps. Harper is telling the truth: under American English
# `haematology` really is the wrong spelling, and it suggests `hematology`.
# Adding a word like this to a pack does nothing, because Harper's dialect check
# never consults pack dictionaries — the lint survives and the pack carries a
# dead entry.
#
# The trap is that probing a single dialect makes these look identical to a
# genuine gap like `kubelet`. Only `--dialect all` separates them: a real gap is
# flagged in all five, a dialect variant in some but not all. test/packs.test.js
# asserts exactly that, so the distinction stays pinned.
#
# Verified 2026-07-25. The comments record which dialects flagged each word at
# the time; the test asserts "some but not all", never a specific list, because
# the specific list is Harper's business and may change.

haematology     # american, canadian
aetiology       # american, canadian
immunisation    # american, canadian
paediatrics     # american
neighbourhood   # american
pediatrics      # british, australian, canadian, indian
